title: Knots
about: Four knots that cover almost everything outdoors: joining, loops, tying to a tree, and tight lines.

articles.title: Reef knot (joining two ends)
articles.intro: Ties two ends of the same rope together, like a bandage or a bundle. Flat and easy to undo.
steps: Hold one end in each hand.
Cross the left end over the right and tuck it under (like the first step of tying shoes).
Now cross the right end over the left and tuck it under.
Pull both ends: the two loops lie flat, side by side.
Remember: left over right, then right over left.
avoid: Don't use it to join two different ropes or to hold a person's weight: it can slip.
If the loops look twisted (a 'granny knot'), untie and redo the second cross the other way.

articles.title: Bowline (a loop that won't slip)
articles.intro: Makes a fixed loop at the end of a rope, for rescue, mooring or hanging. Easy to untie even after a heavy load.
steps: Make a small loop in the rope, with the short end on top (the 'rabbit hole').
Bring the short end up through the loop from below (the rabbit comes out of the hole).
Pass it behind the long part of the rope (round the tree).
Bring it back down through the small loop (back down the hole).
Hold the short end against the big loop and pull the long part tight.
Leave at least a hand's width of tail.
avoid: Don't leave a short tail: it can work loose when not loaded.
Check the knot before trusting your weight to it.

articles.title: Clove hitch (tying to a post or tree)
articles.intro: Quickly ties a rope to a pole, branch or tree, for a ridge line, a tarp or a tent guy.
steps: Wrap the rope once around the post.
Cross over the first wrap and go around the post again.
Tuck the end under that second wrap.
Pull both ends: two neat parallel wraps with an X across them.
avoid: Don't rely on it alone for a load that moves back and forth: add two half hitches.

articles.title: Taut-line hitch (adjustable tight line)
articles.intro: A loop you can slide to tighten or loosen a line: perfect for tent and tarp guy lines.
steps: Pass the rope around a peg or tree and bring the end back along the line.
Wrap the end twice around the line, working towards the peg.
Then wrap once more around the line, outside the first two wraps.
Pull tight. Slide the knot to adjust the tension; it grips when loaded.
avoid: Don't use thin slippery cord: it may not grip.
